# FDG4060

> CONSIDER applying `ComVisible(false)` to your assembly. COM-callable APIs need to be designed explicitly. As a rule of thumb, .NET assemblies should not be visible to COM. If you do design the APIs to be COM-callable, you can apply `ComVisible(true)` either to the individual APIs or to the whole assembly.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.10 Types and Assembly Metadata.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1017
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Library only: COM visibility concerns assemblies that other code loads. CA1017 reports an assembly with no ComVisibleAttribute, without a source location, but with SDK 10.0.402 only when the assembly has an externally visible type in the global namespace; assemblies whose public types are all in namespaces are not reported. CA1017 has no code fix.
